description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from the Whisper large-v3 model after applying various cumulative automated optimisation steps, comparing performance between two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists five optimisation categories—“Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates”—ordered from top to bottom, while the horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” scaled from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035. Each optimisation category has two adjacent horizontal bars, one for each model, with exact WER difference values labeled at the end of each bar. For “Normalised,” the NESAC model shows a WER difference of 0.00334 and the SESHA model 0.00323; for “Add Spacing,” 0.00319 and 0.00344 respectively; for “Remove Spacing,” 0.00311 and 0.00306; for “Americanisms,” 0.00299 and 0.00302; and for “Dates,” 0.00257 and 0.00228. The bars are not sorted by magnitude, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding. The chart visually conveys that while both models improve relative to Whisper large-v3, their performance varies across optimisation types, with SESHA performing better in “Add Spacing” and “Dates,” and NESAC slightly better in “Normalised” and “Remove Spacing.”
